response.markdown_report:
The next experiment should test **supervised recent-context augmentation within one BERT4Rec model**, keeping supervision weights fixed.

**Insights from the starting point.** (1) Endpoint reconstruction matches appended-mask inference’s lack of right context. Weighting matters only when algebraically distinct from the baseline. (2) Electronics’ 13.6% diagnostic wrong-ranking rate identifies weak training-mask separation, without establishing its cause or validation performance. (3) Qualitative feedback motivates prioritizing recent connections. Ownership, compatibility and current demand remain unobserved.

**Insights from related work.** (1) [BERT4Rec](https://arxiv.org/abs/1904.06690) already uses endpoint masking; its implementation includes segmentation. Neither mechanism is new. (2) [CL4SRec](https://arxiv.org/abs/2010.14395) shows that context augmentation can help without selectively retaining recent history. Thus generic regularization is an alternative explanation. (3) [Does It Look Sequential?](https://arxiv.org/abs/2408.12008) motivates history-sensitivity tests, while [sampling pitfalls](https://hidasi.eu/assets/pdf/eval_flaws_recsys23.pdf) require keeping auxiliary probes separate from pinned evaluation.

**Framework.** Three directions separate interventions from evidence:

| Direction | Minimal intervention | Evidence and remaining gap |
|---|---|---|
| Supervision allocation | Endpoint weight 0.75 | Tests allocation; cannot isolate context mismatch |
| Context availability | Shorten endpoint history | Tests augmentation; matched short controls distinguish recency |
| Behavioral diagnosis | Matched recent/older removals | Measures sensitivity; cannot verify current intent |

**Candidate assessments.** Scores are originality/potential/difficulty; higher difficulty means harder implementation.

- **Endpoint weight 0.75 — 2/5/3.** Originality: useful control, established weighting. Potential: inexpensive evidence, heuristic coefficient. Difficulty: small edit, careful reductions.
- **Recent-context augmentation — 3/6/4.** Originality: specific endpoint application, established cropping. Potential: tests history-horizon robustness, risks popularity shortcuts. Difficulty: simple sampler change, demanding position and padding controls.
- **Matched history-removal probe — 3/6/4.** Originality: informative comparison, established perturbations. Potential: guides interventions, offers no direct accuracy gain. Difficulty: reuses inference, requires positional controls.

**Selected experiment.** At 10% progress, retain recent-context augmentation. For explicitly generated endpoint examples, keep the latest ten preceding interactions with probability 0.25; otherwise preserve context. Keep reconstruction examples, reductions and weights unchanged. Compare with the exact baseline using matched targets and updates. If budget permits, add a count-matched random-subset training control; without it, attribute gains only to augmentation, not recency.

```python
x, labels = baseline_endpoint_example()  # fixed width; target is MASK
positions = baseline_position_ids(x)
if augmentation_rng.random() < 0.25:
    x = pad_history_except_latest(x, keep=10)  # preserve columns
loss = unchanged_objective(x, positions, labels, reconstruction_group)
```

Preserve retained-token/MASK position IDs, mask padding keys at every layer, and ignore padded queries in loss. Verify padding-content invariance, final-nonpadding readout and predictor parity. Cumulative position IDs require computing IDs before removal and compatible explicit-position handling. Keep full-history inference and measure its validation performance directly. Retain all categories, seeds, limits, diagnostic interfaces and one checkpoint/category. Select solely by host macro validation HR@10 within budget. No improvement is established.

idea.description: Test supervised recent-context augmentation for endpoint supervision within each category’s single corrected BERT4Rec model. With probability 0.25, retain only the latest ten observed interactions preceding an endpoint target; otherwise retain the baseline context. Keep ordinary reconstruction supervision, objective weights and deployed full-context inference unchanged.
idea.motivation: The qualitative diagnosis suggests that broad historical associations sometimes outrank direct recent-interest connections. Shortened endpoint contexts provide a small intervention using observed histories, without treating recency as evidence of current demand. This changes context availability while holding supervision allocation fixed. CL4SRec supplies precedent for generic augmentation benefits, so an improvement alone would not identify recency as its mechanism.
idea.implementation_notes:
Use the supplied corrected baseline as the exact control. Its source is absent from this input, so this remains an implementation specification rather than an executable replacement train.py. First document its endpoint provenance, target sampling, reconstruction policy, position convention, padding attention, exact loss reductions and optimizer construction. Apply augmentation only to explicitly generated endpoint examples. If introducing those examples changes the baseline, include a matched-construction control before attributing differences to cropping; reduce the comparison set if controls exceed the remaining budget. Omit the candidate if all eligible contexts contain at most ten preceding interactions.

Fix recent_length=10 and augmentation_probability=0.25 before validation. Draw the augmentation Bernoulli for every endpoint example; examples with at most ten preceding interactions remain unchanged. Record both selected and actually changed fractions. Preserve target draws, reconstruction masks, group membership, loss denominators, group weights, optimizer, batch size, update counts and validation schedule across comparison arms. Use separate deterministic augmentation randomness initialized from seed 42, independent of baseline sampling and model dropout randomness. A concrete implementation can key augmentation draws by category index, epoch, step and example index, using a documented deterministic seed construction.

Construct the baseline fixed-width, left-padded endpoint input with room reserved for its MASK before removing context. For selected examples, replace all but the latest ten preceding valid history tokens with PAD in their original columns; leave MASK, its label and all retained columns unchanged. Keep padding and unsupervised labels ignored. The selected target occurrence must be replaced by MASK, with its identity supplied only as a label. Legitimate earlier interactions with the same item may remain; do not remove repeated IDs or change target sampling. Every supervised input position must contain the reserved MASK.

For absolute column positions, retaining the original width and columns preserves positions. If positions use cumulative nonpadding counts or another input-dependent rule, compute original position IDs before removal and pass them explicitly without renumbering retained tokens. This may require an optional position_ids argument while preserving log2feats(sequence) compatibility and baseline default behavior; serialize any relevant configuration and update the embedded predictor writer consistently. Do not silently switch the baseline position convention. Relative attention also requires checking for absolute components and changed distance definitions.

Mask padded keys in every attention layer; a zero PAD embedding alone is insufficient. Keep MASK valid and exclude padded query outputs from loss and readout. In evaluation mode, verify retained-token and MASK positions match the uncropped reference, finite valid outputs persist, and changing values at padding locations under an unchanged explicit padding mask leaves valid outputs unchanged. If the model derives padding masks from IDs, test padding invariance by perturbing masked hidden states or embeddings rather than turning PAD IDs into valid items. Do not require cropped and uncropped predictions to match: context removal is the intervention.

Inference retains the baseline full allowed history, appends MASK, left-pads and reads the actual final nonpadding column, never count-1. Train and predictor preprocessing, position construction and scoring must match. Check checkpoint round-trip and predictor score parity. Cropped-training/full-inference performance is an empirical question, not a guaranteed augmentation benefit.

The minimum accuracy comparison is exact baseline versus suffix augmentation. If predeclared compute remains, train a count-matched random-subset control with identical augmentation selections and targets: uniformly retain ten preceding valid positions without replacement, preserve their original order and position IDs, and use full context otherwise. This control separates preferential retention of recent events from generic context removal only partially, because retained spacing also differs. Old-prefix and random-contiguous controls, crossed cropped/full inference, and timestamp-versus-event-count horizons are future experiments rather than mandatory additions. Without suitable controls, report any gain as augmentation-associated and avoid causal recency claims. Ten interactions describe an event-count horizon, not elapsed time.

Retain one independently trained checkpoint per category, all four dataset routes, DATA_DIR = os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR'], trial-local artifacts, preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, at most 200 epochs and 200 batches per epoch, and single-GPU execution. No independently fitted experts, score fusion, checkpoint averaging, external weights or unavailable attributes are introduced. Preserve ModelView interfaces, including the actual view.model module, item_emb, log2feats(sequence), predict_score(features, items), user_train, meta_data and review_data. DiagnosisProbe(view, device).run_full_diagnosis(train_loader) must return metrics and metric_definitions; diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis) must use measured values and definitions. Retain B x L diagnostic batches and measure only valid supervised MASK positions. Existing training-mask margins are auxiliary and cannot identify HR@10 gains or recommendation diversity.

Predeclare comparison arms, matched completed-update targets and maximum GPU-time allocations within the remaining shared 43,200 GPU-second budget, including training, validation, diagnosis and failures. Record completed updates, context lengths, supervised-target counts, clipping frequency if used, and actual compute; disclose unequal completion. Select exclusively by the pinned four-category macro validation HR@10 with 200 validation users/category, 99 unique negatives and evaluation seed 42. When paired host hits are available, report paired user bootstrap uncertainty within categories with fixed candidates, then equally average category deltas. These intervals exclude seed variation and adaptive search bias. Report every validation query and freeze the final configuration before held-out evaluation. Inspect frequency and history-length strata with counts where available to detect possible popularity shortcuts, without changing selection. Do not infer ownership, fulfilled needs, compatibility or willingness to choose now from interactions. No empirical improvement is claimed.
idea.pseudocode:
spec = document_corrected_baseline()
plan = predeclare_exact_control_and_suffix_augmentation()
# Require a matched-construction control if explicit endpoint groups are introduced.
# Optional random-subset control is included only if predeclared compute permits.
plan.omit_noop_and_duplicate_arms()
plan.allocate_remaining_shared_budget_including_diagnostics()

for arm in plan:
    for category in four_categories:
        model = initialize_corrected_bert4rec(seed=42)
        sampling = reset_matched_baseline_sampling_stream(category)
        for epoch in range(max_epochs_at_most_200):
            for step in range(200):
                stop_if_predeclared_compute_allocation_exhausted()
                batch = sampling.draw_arm_appropriate_batch(arm)
                for index, example in enumerate(batch.explicit_endpoint_examples):
                    # Build reference before context removal; reserve space for MASK.
                    reference = spec.build_endpoint_input(example)
                    positions = spec.position_ids(reference.sequence)
                    selected = deterministic_bernoulli(
                        seed=42, category=category, epoch=epoch,
                        step=step, example_index=index, probability=0.25)
                    history_columns = valid_preceding_history_columns(reference)
                    keep = history_columns
                    if selected and arm == 'suffix_augmentation':
                        keep = history_columns[-10:]
                    elif selected and arm == 'random_subset_control':
                        keep = sorted(deterministic_uniform_subset(
                            history_columns, size=min(10, len(history_columns))))
                    example = replace_removed_history_with_PAD(
                        reference, keep_columns=keep)
                    example.position_ids = positions
                    assert_retained_positions_and_MASK_match(reference, example)
                    assert_ignored_labels_at_padding_and_unsupervised_columns(example)
                assert_supervised_inputs_are_reserved_MASK(batch)
                # Padding keys are blocked at every layer; MASK remains valid.
                loss = spec.unchanged_objective(model, batch)
                optimizer.zero_grad()
                loss.backward()
                optimizer.step()
                record_counts_context_lengths_updates_and_compute()
        verify_padding_invariance_and_final_nonpadding_readout(model)
        save_one_checkpoint_and_matching_predictor(model, category)
        verify_checkpoint_roundtrip_and_predictor_score_parity()

# Evaluate full-history appended-MASK inference with the unchanged host evaluator.
# Select solely using four-category macro validation HR@10.
# Without matched short-context controls, interpret gains as augmentation-associated.
# Freeze the final configuration before held-out inference.
# Deploy exactly one trained checkpoint per category.

originality.positive: The endpoint-only suffix intervention and controlled interaction with ordinary Cloze supervision form a specific, testable application to the supplied diagnosis.
originality.negative: Cropping, supervised augmentation, endpoint masking and unchanged full-context inference have established precedents; priority for their exact combination is unverified.

future_potential.positive: A controlled result could motivate studies of context horizons and inference robustness within one BERT4Rec encoder, with clear comparisons against generic augmentation.
future_potential.negative: Cropping can discard persistent interests or encourage popularity shortcuts, and a validation gain would not establish improved compatibility, current demand or a recency mechanism.

code_difficulty.positive: The core intervention changes endpoint input construction while retaining the backbone, recommendation objective and deployed scoring.
code_difficulty.negative: Position preservation, attention masking, deterministic matched sampling and predictor parity require careful integration; input-dependent position conventions or missing endpoint groups increase scope.

related_work.title: BERT4Rec: Sequential Recommendation with Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformer
contributions: Uses bidirectional masked-item reconstruction, endpoint masking and appended-mask next-item prediction.
Provides the established supervision setting for the proposed context intervention.
limitations: Does not establish that the proposed cropping probability or history length improves this benchmark.
Interior reconstruction and endpoint inference have different available contexts.

related_work.title: Original BERT4Rec implementation: modeling and training-data generation
contributions: modeling.py implements learned absolute column positions.
gen_data.py supplies precedent for sliding windows, repeated masking and forced last-item masking.
limitations: The corrected host baseline must be documented directly rather than assumed identical to this implementation.
Historical segmentation does not establish the benefit or novelty of endpoint-fixed recent-suffix augmentation.

related_work.title: Contrastive Learning for Sequential Recommendation (CL4SRec)
contributions: Studies crop, mask and reorder augmentations, including plain augmentation comparisons and contrastive training.
Provides a generic regularization explanation that motivates matched short-context controls.
limitations: Random contiguous cropping need not retain the latest interaction.
Its contrastive objective differs from directly supervising the original endpoint target after suffix removal.
Reported gains do not establish a recency mechanism or transfer to this benchmark.

related_work.title: Contrastive Learning for Representation Degeneration Problem in Sequential Recommendation (DuoRec)
contributions: Uses dropout-based views and sequences sharing a next-item target as contrastive positives.
Helps distinguish supervised positive selection for contrastive learning from the proposed supervised context-length augmentation.
limitations: Recent-suffix cropping is not its defining augmentation.
Its additional representation-alignment objective is outside the selected minimal intervention.

related_work.title: Contrastive Learning with Bidirectional Transformers for Sequential Recommendation (CBiT)
contributions: Combines sliding-window sequence construction, Cloze masking and dropout views.
Jointly optimizes masked reconstruction and a dynamically weighted contrastive objective.
limitations: Multiple mechanisms differ from the proposed endpoint-only context intervention.
Historical windows and endpoint-fixed suffix-length variation are distinct constructions.

related_work.title: Does It Look Sequential?
contributions: Examines history-order dependence across sequential recommendation datasets.
Motivates checking behavioral sensitivity before interpreting predictions.
limitations: Order perturbations do not verify current user intent.
Its findings do not determine the best context horizon for these four datasets.

related_work.title: Sampling pitfalls in recommender-system evaluation
contributions: Documents evaluation distortions and model-order changes associated with candidate sampling.
limitations: Provides evaluation guidance rather than an endpoint-training algorithm.
Does not justify modifying the pinned host evaluator.

related_work.title: PyTorch MultiheadAttention documentation
contributions: Specifies that a Boolean key_padding_mask value of True blocks the corresponding key.
Supports implementation checks that distinguish zero PAD embeddings from attention exclusion.
limitations: Other attention APIs can use different Boolean mask conventions.
Correct padding handling does not itself validate the proposed augmentation.
